body:
> Found within minutes of #109 shipping: the first thing tried was drawing the track that had just finished, and it could not be drawn.

## Why

`hkb graph <n>` walks `fetchBoard(ctx)` (`src/cli.js:301`), which returns **open** issues only. `resolveTrack`
then finds no root and the command exits:

```
$ hkb graph 98 --mermaid
hkb: no open task #98 on board "default" — `hkb list` shows what is there
```

#98 is a completed track: a root and four children, decomposed, run and merged in one evening. That is
precisely the graph a human wants to look at — for a retrospective, for a PR description, for showing
someone how a track went. While the work is *in flight* you mostly care about what is ready next, which
the board already tells you; once it is done, the shape is the interesting artefact, and it is exactly
then that the command stops working.

The restriction looks inherited rather than chosen: `hkb list --all` already reads closed tasks, so the
data is there and the walk is the same.

## What

Let `hkb graph` draw a finished track.

- Read closed tasks too when resolving the graph — reuse whatever `hkb list --all` does rather than
  adding a second fetch path.
- Keep the default cheap. If including closed tasks costs a bigger query, make it `--all` (mirroring
  `hkb list`) and have the current error name that flag instead of just pointing at `hkb list`:
  `no open task #98 — it may be finished; try \`hkb graph 98 --all\``.
- Done nodes must be visually distinguishable in the mermaid output, the way the board already
  distinguishes them — a `done` classDef, so a finished track does not render as though it were pending.

## Done when

- [ ] `hkb graph 98 --mermaid` (or `--all`) emits the four-child diamond for the completed track #98.
- [ ] A closed node renders visibly different from an open one.
- [ ] The error for a genuinely unknown number still says what to do next, and does not suggest a flag
      that will not help.
- [ ] `--json` carries the same nodes/edges as the mermaid form, with each node's status.
- [ ] `node --test test/track.test.js` covers a track whose root and children are all closed.
goal: hkb graph draws a completed track, with done nodes visually distinct
title: hkb graph refuses a finished track, which is the one you most want to draw
